title: TFLite Micro libraries and useful examples

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “TFLite Micro libraries and useful examples” correctly?
options: TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) is a small C/C++ runtime for running a prepared TensorFlow Lite model on a microcontroller, often without internet.
We usually do not train a model on the microcontroller itself.
TFLite Micro does not create a model
IoT devices connect to a network and send data.
questions.answer: TFLite Micro does not create a model
questions.explanation: TFLite Micro does not create a model

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “TFLite Micro libraries and useful examples” is accurate?
options: It does not train the model
Collect and label examples on a computer, train and evaluate a small model there, then convert it to a supported format and run inference on the board.
it is the runtime and supporting C/C++ library used to execute a prepared model.
AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things) adds machine-learning decisions: a device can interpret sensor readings instead of only forwarding them.
questions.answer: it is the runtime and supporting C/C++ library used to execute a prepared model.
questions.explanation: it is the runtime and supporting C/C++ library used to execute a prepared model.

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “TFLite Micro libraries and useful examples”?
options: For example, a microphone can recognize a simple clap locally, or a vibration sensor can flag a pattern that may indicate a machine problem.
training and conversion usually happen on a computer.
Train and convert on a computer, then run inference on the device.
A simple path: 1) read the sensor correctly
questions.answer: Train and convert on a computer, then run inference on the device.
questions.explanation: Train and convert on a computer, then run inference on the device.
